classification.difficultyReason: Carry out a specified open circle/chord construction and recognise the taught same-arc equality in two explicitly prompted minor/major configurations; familiar construction plus comparison, no hidden proof strategy.

content.prompt: Points labelled O in this exercise are always centres of circles.

children.label: a
children.prompt: Draw a large circle, and draw a chord AB that is not a diameter.

answer.short: Sample construction: a circle and a chord AB that does not pass through its centre.
answer.worked: Draw a large circle. Choose A and B on its circumference so that AB does not pass through the centre, then join AB. Retain the drawing for both pairs of angles.

children.label: b
children.prompt: Draw two angles at the circumference standing on the minor arc AB. How are these two angles related?

answer.worked: Choose distinct points P and Q on the major arc AB. Join each of them to A and B, so $\angle APB$ and $\angle AQB$ stand on the same minor arc AB. Angles at the circumference standing on the same arc are equal. Equivalently, each is half the same smaller central angle.

spec.description: Editable complete sample: non-diameter chordAB with distinct P/Q on majorarc; both marked inscribed angles stand on minorarcAB and are equal.
spec.answerVisibility: Sample answer only. No supplied student given or fixed measurement added.

children.label: c
children.prompt: Draw two angles at the circumference standing on the major arc AB. How are these two angles related?

answer.worked: Choose two distinct points P and Q on the minor arc AB. Join each to A and B. Now $\angle APB$ and $\angle AQB$ both stand on the same major arc AB, so they are equal. Each is half the same reflex central angle; the theorem applies to major arcs too.

spec.description: Editable complete sample: same non-diameter chordAB with distinct P/Q on minorarc; both interior obtuse angles stand on majorarcAB and are equal.
